subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement an enforced default boundary, keep it opt-in through `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandboxing, or route the remaining work to a broader path-policy/sandbox design?
rationale: The decision changes a security boundary and compatibility-sensitive default across file tools, shell execution, and multi-agent workflows, so source inspection alone cannot choose the product policy safely.

options.title: Define an enforced default boundary
options.body: Choose the intended default confinement semantics, migration/docs plan, and exec behavior before merging a filesystem policy change.

options.title: Keep confinement opt-in
options.body: Document `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandboxing as the supported current boundary while routing stricter defaults to separate product work.

options.title: Defer to broader sandbox design
options.body: Treat this issue as blocked on the unified sandbox or local-user isolation trackers rather than landing a file-tool-only change.

recommendation.title: Define an enforced default boundary
recommendation.body: Choose the intended default confinement semantics, migration/docs plan, and exec behavior before merging a filesystem policy change.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history on the workspaceOnly policy and prior filesystem-security reviews.
